note: fork F3A -- the arm-log order gate. Edit ONLY with a --compare verdict in the same commit saying which steps moved and why. THE FIFTH BASELINE, recorded by fork F4F (2026-09-13), closing a deferral that had stood since F3 as `measure it when a netoff lane is first routine`. It still is not routine -- NO gate unit produces this key; the only enable=0 lanes in the tree are hand-run (the inmem parity lane, which F4C-GATE owns) -- so this file exists to give the next such run a VERDICT instead of a refusal, not because anything re-measures it. WHAT IT IS: identical to brokered.json except step #28, `check_arm_order --compare f4f_bound f4f_netoff` = SURVIVOR ORDER IDENTICAL, 1 text change, 71 vs 71 structural lines. KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than pre-populated: this was recorded from a PLAIN lane, so unlike brokered.json it carries no optional [inmem] steps and no harness `alt` texts. A netoff lane that also arms the harness or the in-memory patcher will therefore red as an INSERT -- that is a shape nobody has measured, and the fix is to measure it and add the entries with a --compare verdict, exactly as F3G and F4F did for the other two files. Do not copy brokered.json's annotations across on the assumption that they hold here.
recipe: python tools/make_lane.py --name f4f_netoff --lane 97 --port 6597 --headless && set [net] enable=0 IN THE EXISTING [net] SECTION of the lane's mh_net.ini (make_lane --extra-ini APPENDS a second [net] section and GetPrivateProfile takes the FIRST -- an appended enable=0 is silently ignored, measured 2026-09-13), then launch mh.focus.exe --skip-intro from the lane dir and kill it at the menu -- fork F4F recorded the FIFTH baseline this way, from a PLAIN lane with all three satellites deployed.
